eth:halt.note: no exit and no liquidation while the chain is halted

ethena:shortfall.note: USDe loses backing; the oracle follows only after the meta-oracle switches to its USDe / USD backup (deviation above threshold for the challenge timelock)

usde:depeg.note: USDe falls against USD: the PT is denominated in USDe, so it falls by the same share; USDe / USD is priced only by the backup oracle, which takes over after the meta-oracle switch

susde:navLoss.note: sUSDe's NAV (USDe per sUSDe = totalAssets / totalSupply) falls: the SY exchange rate falls with it and the PT index never decreases (max of rate and stored index), so PT holders lose the same share for good (Pendle PendleERC4626SY / PendleYieldToken source). No feed prices sUSDe's NAV, so nobody is liquidated and lenders' bad debt builds silently

susde:discount.note: sUSDe trades below its NAV on markets while the NAV is unchanged: the PT still redeems at the NAV-based rate, so holding to expiry recovers it; selling now would lock in the loss

feeds:oracleLow.note: the feed reports the low price itself; the price recovers but liquidations stay

feeds:stale.note: liquidations use the last price; the PT feed is computed every block and cannot go stale, the USDe / USD feed can

oracle:oracleLow.note: the oracle reports the low price itself; the price recovers but liquidations stay

oracle:stale.note: liquidations use the last price until it updates

market:drain.note: pool liquidity removed is the severity (assumption): sellable = max_exit_fraction x (1 - d), each sale costs what a sale 1/(1-d) times larger costs today

pt:depeg.note: the PT market price falls; the oracle prices the PT by a linear discount (no market input), and the PT still redeems at expiry, so holding to expiry recovers it

lending:cascade.note: other borrowers are liquidated and their PT is sold into the pool first; severity = oracle drop that liquidates them (borrowers.exit_later). The PT market price alone does not move this oracle
